This was his third hospitalization with the same presentation of small bowel obstruction, with previous admissions one month ago and 2 weeks ago. knowledge_fragments.content: Presentation: A 74-year-old female with a history of adrenal insufficiency, diabetes mellitus, and hypothyroidism presented with severe nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain for a week. On admission, her vital signs were within normal range. The physical exam revealed generalized abdominal tenderness without rebound or guarding. Laboratory results showed mild hyponatremia (Na: 132 mmol/L) but were otherwise normal. A computed tomography (CT) of the abdomen indicated high-grade small bowel obstruction with a possible transition in the right pelvis. Multiple masses were observed throughout the abdomen and pelvis, consistent with peritoneal studding, and a possible primary mass in the right pelvic region. A nasogastric tube was placed at the bedside for decompression. Tumor markers revealed a CA-125 antigen slightly elevated to 67.2 U/ml (range 0-35 U/ml); CA-19-9 and CEA antigens were normal. The patient has not been deemed a candidate for surgical intervention due to the extensive disease observed during surgical evaluation.. Confirmed diagnosis: Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor. Differential diagnosis includes: Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor.
knowledge_fragments.title: Case report: Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor

knowledge_fragments.content: Presentation: A 24-year-old male presents with nausea, vomiting, and weight loss. Over the past year, he experienced intermittent nausea and vomiting, resulting in a weight reduction of 15 kg (from 82 kg to 67 kg) despite maintaining a normal appetite. His height is 170.7 cm. Initially, he aimed to lose weight due to concerns about his body image, with an ideal weight goal of 65 kg. An upper gastrointestinal endoscopy performed at another clinic showed normal findings, and medication for gastrointestinal motility did not alleviate his symptoms. He was referred to our department with a previous diagnosis of an eating disorder. During observation post-admission, he occasionally vomited unexpectedly while at other times he could swallow food without issues, indicating that the vomiting was not self-induced.. Confirmed diagnosis: esophageal achalasia. Differential diagnosis includes: esophageal achalasia.

knowledge_fragments.content: Presentation: A 30-year-old male patient arrived at the emergency department with severe abdominal pain, diarrhea, and vomiting that had persisted for 24 hours. The patient mentioned experiencing a similar episode three months earlier, which was managed conservatively at another facility. His medical history includes posttraumatic stress disorder and chronic cannabis use, consuming 10-15 joints daily. The pain was so intense that the patient was observed by his girlfriend pouring boiling water on himself. Upon admission, the patient exhibited aggressive behavior, posing a risk to himself and others. Blood tests revealed an elevated leucocyte count of 16.88 G/l, while the C-reactive protein level was normal at 0.1 mg/dl. Initial treatment included lorazepam and olanzapine.. Confirmed diagnosis: Multiple intestinal intussusceptions caused by highly impaired gastrointestinal motility. Differential diagnosis includes: Multiple intestinal intussusceptions caused by highly impaired gastrointestinal motility.
knowledge_fragments.title: Case report: Multiple intestinal intussusceptions caused by highly impaired gastrointestinal motility

knowledge_fragments.content: Presentation: In 2011, a 48-year-old woman presented with multiple new calcifications in the skin of her back, hips, and shoulders. These calcifications remained stable over the next 5 years. In 2015, she developed symptoms consistent with Raynaud syndrome, and firm plaques were observed on her skin. By March 2016, her condition had worsened, showing edema of the fingers ('puffy fingers'). Radiography confirmed the presence of skin calcifications. Treatment was initiated with systemic prostaglandins, bisphosphonates, and D-penicillamine. After 2 years of treatment, the calcifications reduced in size, but the symptoms of Raynaud syndrome persisted, leading to the prescription of bosentan.. Confirmed diagnosis: CREST syndrome with esophageal motility disorder. Differential diagnosis includes: CREST syndrome with esophageal motility disorder.

knowledge_fragments.content: 염증성 장질환(inflammatory bowel disease; 이하 IBD)은 원인을 알 수 없는 장의 만성 염증상태를 가지는 질환군이다. 염증성 장질환의 두 가지 주요 질환으로 크론병(Crohn’s disease)과 궤양성 대장염(ulcerative colitis)이 있으며, 이 두 질환의 임상 양상과 병리 소견은 구분되기도 하며 일부 겹치기도 한다. 여러 연구에서 유전적 및 환경적 요인에 의한 장 면역의 조절 장애에 따른 위장의 손상이 원인으로 생각되고 있으나 아직까지 병태생리에 대한 이해는 불완전하다.

knowledge_fragments.content: Presentation: A 48-year-old male reported experiencing weight loss and obstipation over the past two months. He did not report any episodes of diarrhea, hematochezia, or abdominal pain. His medical history was negative for inflammatory bowel disease, skin disease, thyroid cancer, and genital cancer. There was no family history of inflammatory bowel disease or colon cancer. Physical examination and laboratory tests yielded normal results. No verrucous lesions, skin pigmentation, alopecia, or onychodystrophy were observed.. Confirmed diagnosis: Hamartomatous Polyps. Differential diagnosis includes: Hamartomatous Polyps.

Despite treatment, she continued to experience symptoms and had a significant weight loss of 20 kg over 4 months.. Confirmed diagnosis: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma. knowledge_fragments.content: The prevalence of inflammatory bowel disease is steadily increasing in Korea, and there is growing interest among doctors in its treatment. Practitioners should be well informed of the colonoscopically diagnosable lesions in order to prevent misidentification of other diseases as inflammatory bowel disease, leading to overtreatment and to avoid misdiagnosis, which could delay treatment. Effort is needed to carefully select treatment approach appropriate for each patient by providing a precise diagnosis on the extent and degree of lesions as well as to accurately delineate the lesions to assure that they are compared in subsequent rounds of follow-up monitoring in order to allow redetermination and adjustment of treatment.
knowledge_fragments.title: Differential diagnosis of inflammatory bowel disease: what is the role of colonoscopy? > CONCLUSIONS

knowledge_fragments.content: Presentation: A 16-year-old male was admitted in June 2021 presenting with bloody diarrhea, fever, and cough for approximately one week. The patient also reported difficulty swallowing and rhinitis. His medical history was unremarkable. Physical examination revealed eyelid edema, bilateral non-purulent conjunctivitis, strawberry tongue, swollen lips, and oral ulcerations. Laboratory findings included leukocytosis with lymphopenia, significantly elevated ESR and C-reactive protein, elevated ferritin, D-dimers, mild elevation of alanine aminotransferase, and γ-glutamyltransferase. SARS-CoV-2 antibodies were positive for IgG and negative for IgM. The patient was treated with IVIG and ASA, but symptoms persisted. Steroid therapy was initiated, leading to a gradual resolution of symptoms. Approximately one month later, during steroid tapering, the patient experienced a recurrence of bloody diarrhea, along with eyelid edema and bilateral non-purulent conjunctivitis.. Confirmed diagnosis: Inflammatory Bowel Disease type unclassified. Differential diagnosis includes: Inflammatory Bowel Disease type unclassified.
knowledge_fragments.title: Case report: Inflammatory Bowel Disease type unclassified

knowledge_fragments.content: Presentation: A 38-year-old woman presented to the Emergency Department with acute severe lower back pain, fever, nausea, and vomiting. Her medical history included recurrent urinary infections and kidney stones. She was undergoing evaluation in the genetic department due to her history of infertility, multiple spontaneous abortions, and a family history of sudden deaths, including her father. On physical examination, she exhibited translucent skin, a thin nose, and joint hypermobility in the lower limbs. Laboratory results showed a hemoglobin level of 13 g/dL, leukocytosis at 16 × 10^9/L, and an elevated C-reactive protein level of 54 mg/dL. Urinary sediment was inactive. Renal ultrasound revealed perirenal fluid and indications of nephritis without any obstruction.. Confirmed diagnosis: Vascular Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome. Differential diagnosis includes: Vascular Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome.

knowledge_fragments.content: Presentation: A 20-year-old female patient presented with abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. Physical examination showed mild hypotension and a distended, tender abdomen. Vital signs included a temperature of 37.9°C, a heart rate of 98 beats per minute, and a blood pressure of 97/49 mm Hg. Laboratory results indicated a white blood cell count of 12,250/mm3. A computed tomography scan revealed significant dilatation of the sigmoid colon with intraperitoneal fluid. An emergent laparotomy identified dilatation of the sigmoid colon, breakdown of the serosa and muscularis propria of the sigmoid colon with impending perforation, and intra-abdominal hemorrhage due to breakdown of the mesenterium of the sigmoid colon. The rest of the intestine appeared normal, leading to the resection of the sigmoid colon with Hartmann's pouch and an end colostomy. The resected colon exhibited strong alteration of the bowel wall, with some areas lacking the lamina muscularis propria. Histological examination of the resected specimen showed mucosal necrosis with leukocytic infiltration. (For nausea and vomiting in infants and children, see p.

.)

Nausea, the unpleasant feeling of needing to vomit, represents awareness of afferent stimuli (including

increased parasympathetic tone) to the medullary vomiting center. Vomiting is the forceful expulsion of

gastric contents caused by involuntary contraction of the abdominal musculature when the gastric fundus

and lower esophageal sphincter are relaxed.

Vomiting should be distinguished from regurgitation, the spitting up of gastric contents without associated

nausea or forceful abdominal muscular contractions. Patients with achalasia or a Zenker's diverticulum

may regurgitate undigested food without nausea.

The patient's symptoms of nausea and vomiting, worsened by large fatty meals and alcohol, along with the physical exam findings of an obese, tympanitic, and distended abdomen, are consistent with a gastrointestinal obstruction. The presence of a 3 cm scar in the right lower quadrant of the abdomen suggests a possible incisional hernia, which can cause intestinal obstruction.

The patient's symptoms of nausea and vomiting, worsened by large fatty meals and alcohol, along with the abdominal exam revealing an obese, tympanitic, and distended abdomen, are consistent with a gastrointestinal obstruction. The presence of a 3 cm scar in the right lower quadrant of the abdomen suggests a history of abdominal surgery, which is a common cause of adhesions. Adhesions are a type of mechanical obstruction that can cause the symptoms described.

The patient's symptoms of nausea, vomiting, and abdominal distension, along with the presence of a 3 cm scar in the right lower quadrant, are consistent with an incarcerated hernia, which is a type of gastrointestinal obstruction.

Mesenteric ischemia can cause gastrointestinal obstruction due to decreased blood flow to the intestines, leading to nausea, vomiting, and abdominal distension, which are consistent with the patient's symptoms.

The patient's symptoms of nausea and vomiting, particularly after large fatty meals, and the presence of a distended abdomen, are consistent with gastroparesis, a specific type of gastrointestinal motility disorder.

tree.case_summary:
A 55-year-old man presents to the emergency department with nausea and vomiting for the past week. He decided to come in when his symptoms worsened. He feels that his symptoms are exacerbated with large fatty meals and when he drinks alcohol. His wife recently returned from a cruise with symptoms of vomiting and diarrhea. The patient has a medical history of poorly managed diabetes, constipation, anxiety, dyslipidemia, and hypertension. Abdominal exam reveals an obese, tympanitic and distended abdomen with a 3 cm scar in the right lower quadrant. Vascular exam reveals weak pulses in the lower extremities. Which of the following is the most likely underlying etiology of this patient's symptoms?
